newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at '96 high despite late selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at '96 high despite late selling.

text.p: Taiwan stocks surpassed Monday's 1996 record-high close at the finish on Tuesday, but last-minute profit-taking eroded gains from what brokers suspected was a politically inspired, state-engineered rally.
The weighted index closed up 28.16 points or 0.42 percent at 6,687.88, a new 1996 high close. Turnover was T$69.8 billion.

The index jumped to a 1996 intrasession high of 6,728.64 at one point of the active session, pushed higher by what brokers said appeared to be strong buying by state-controlled funds to mark six months since President Lee Teng-hui's inauguration.
Profit-taking then hit Monday's star sector -- plastics.
"Apparently some investors decided to take the advantage of the government and started taking profits in late trade," said Tank Hung, an analyst of Yuan Ta Securities.
Brokers suspected earlier buying momentum was mainly fuelled by government-related funds.

President Lee, who won a landslide in March in the island's first direct presidential election, was sworn in on May 20 and called at the time for state agencies to boost investment and show concrete results in six months -- roughly now.
Some brokers, suspecting politics, said the stock rise was one of the "concrete results" to demonstrate a healing economy.
Local media reported Taiwan's huge labour pension funds bought some T$2 billion in stocks on Monday.
On Tuedsay, high-technology and shipping shares were strong. Computer giant Acer Inc, the session's most active issue, surged the daily seven percent limit to T$42.8.
Shipping shares rose on expectations of possible easing ties between political rivals Taiwan and China. Yang Ming Marine gained T$1.1 or 3.32 percent to T$34.2.
The ruling Nationalist Party's drafting of a China peace treaty and Lee's renewed invitation to China's communist leaders to visit Taiwan were taken as positive signs, analysts said.
"Today's performance shows that the market needs more time to breach the key 6,700-point resistance," Yuan Ta's Hung said.
The market was likely to consolidate around current levels on Wednesday, brokers added.
